Hi

This is the start to my journal, in which I will document my journey into reading the market. But first a little about me. After looking at some of the posts and threads in this forum I will consider myself a newbie, rookie, green behind the ears. I've been interested in trading for about 18 months, and I can identify all the common errors a trader makes in myself. The connection between my mind and my right index finger, which hits the trigger is often overruled by emotions. About 3 months ago I started looking at PASR, I focused on candle formations on the HTF. Suddenly I found I was starting to make better decisions and I knew their was more to this. My trading style is undefined at this stage, but I do tend to favor the HTF's as screen time is limited. I've decided to take this learning and trading experience seriously, so I'm going to start at the beginning and work my way through all the material do all the homework and practice, practice till its instinctive. Hopefully the teacher here can help me achieve this.

Thank you to all those people that make this site a reality, It is much appreciated!

Ok here is my first exercise I've done based on key levels SR.

What I found interesting while doing the exercise is that if you have to write down what you see, you start thinking about it a lot more than just looking at the chart.

Price open (1) and moved down breaking through the lower major level and continuing to the next major level, here it found strong support and retraced back passed its opening price to the higher major level where it found resistance and closed slightly below this level. This was a significant bullish move. The bullish momentum continued breaking through another major level and found resistance at 1.30400 (2) were it stalled for a day but then continued the bullish momentum breaking this major level as well. The price close just above the minor level (3) 1.30740. Price started ranging over the next few days between two major levels 1.31300 and 1.30400 before breaking down, and closing in no man’s land. (4) Price gained significant bullish momentum breaking the 1.31300 major level but found resistance at the next major level 1.31930. (5) Resistance was obviously very strong and price changed direction with a significant move downwards back to the previous day opening, in the process breaking through 2 major levels. It found support at level 1.29960. Price once again started ranging between 1.30400 and 1.31300 (question to self or others does this mean that these 2 levels are becoming more significant 1.30400 and 1.31300, this is the second time price is ranging between them?). (6) Price eventually moves down breaking the 1.30400 level and closing just below the next major level. (7) It continues down to find support at the next major level before retracing to close above its opening price. Price then tries to make a bullish move but fails and retraces back to close near its opening price. ( Price tries again to move up but finds resistance at 1.30400 before breaking this level which then triggers a significant rally up before price finds resistance at the major level 1.31930 (9). The next day price continues up but doesn’t make it to the next major level before it retraces forming a “falling star” candle formation (indicating to me a trend reversal). (10) Price does react to this formation and moves down to find support at level 1.30400 (we are back at 1.30400 interesting). Once again we find price ranging between 1.31300 and 1.30400 it tests the upper level 1.31300 before breaking it and moving up till it finds resistance at the next major level 1.31930 (11). A decision is made and price starts to fall breaking through 2 major levels before finding support just short of the 3rd major level and comes to close at about 1.30400. (12) The momentum continues down with price breaking through the 1.29970 level and finding support at 1.29500. We have a double top formation; price must break the 1.29500 level for the formation to be confirmed. (13) Price retraces back to the previous major level and eventually closes forming a doji candle (the market is unsure of direction). (14) A decision is made price moves down breaking the 1.29500 level and confirming the double top formation. Price continues down before finding some resistance at 1.28400 and eventually moves down to just short of 1.27900 levels (15). Ok I’m going to stop here and continue tomorrow. From this exercise it seems to me that the levels 1.30400 and 1.31300 are significant, or let’s say have more importance than the other levels at this stage in PA on the chart?

in2forex wrote: In2forex,

I do have a question, If you had taken the trade on the first touch of supply 1 would you have exited the trade when it failed to move below demand 2, or would you not have taken the trade at all as it hadn't engulfed the fresh demand.

You are asking the right questions and seeing the right things. I think the answer has to do with what your expectations are. We "expect" a reaction of some sort at Supply 1 so taking a trade there makes sense. But, you shouldn't then "expect" it to just cruise through demand. And, as you said, when it didn't at least engulf that new demand, it's better to take some or all of your profit. This is something I'm still working on. If you look at my journal you'll see that I took a similar EU short today but didn't take my profit and ended up with a BE.

Also, note on your original trade, you didn't take the 1st visit back to the supply but the 3rd visit. This is something that I had a hard time with since it's nice to see some confirmation that price is reacting where you expect it to. This is where dropping down into the LTF and getting in on a retracement after the initial reaction makes sense.

I had a great moment this last week just on the release of the NFP on Friday. I've would have never looked at the lower time frames before I joined RTM and would never have taken such a trade.

This is how it unfolded. I wasn't planning on taking a trade just watching the EU chart on release of the NFP data. once price started moving bullish I had a sense that it was struggling to go up. I noticed on the 5 Min chart the long tails which was telling me price wanted to go down.

The lows got engulfed and a took a short trade. At this time I didn't have a target so I quickly looked at the history and saw that a supply zone had been ignored. When price started retracing from it I exited.

The significance of this trade for me (even though only 16 pips) was that I trade with no fear, and was using knowledge that I learnt in this forum.

long on EURUSD Preparation = Marked up 4H Demand and Supply zones Set Pending Order long just above the 4H demand zone. Order got triggered My original target was the bottom of the Supply but I exited early, got scared when price briefly reacted to a Flag Limit. Should have watched PA at that point to see if price was going to retrace or push through to my original target. Still lots to learn!!

Last night I was doing some more homework. I was concentrating on RBD's looking how price approached the zone what happened with price in the zone and how to identify an engulf and entry level from that engulf. This morning I noticed an engulf creating a flag limit on EURUSD (I think that what it is?) I waited for price to retrace and the took the buy entry, I had an idea that price wanted to go to the 4H supply which was my target. I had put a PO sell at that level for a FTB to that zone. Waiting to see what happens put Price is ranging just above my entry. Is it a RBD or will it go north. Don't know at this time my stop is above the 4H Supply, but if the range price is in at the moment engulfs north I may exit early, waiting to see which way price goes.

Then it's back to doing more home work!!

Last week I was traveling. On thursday night I didn't have an internet connection so I started drawing my own charts. I wanted to understand what was happening when price moved and why there would be a pool of orders left behind or consumed. I started to realize that RTM isn't as much about trading than it is about what the name says "Read The Market".

If I can identify key areas, If I can identify the significance of those area's, and if I can READ what pro money wants to do, then trading what I see will be easy. Over the last few weeks I've been a sponge to the information on this site. Now its time to put some structure and learning goals to that information,

My journal is no long going to be about what trades I've taken, but more about what I see, how I read what I see. Later I'll come back to trading.

This was an Eureka for me. I wanted to add an Eureka moment quote this is one I liked.

On monday learnt a lession about MT4 and drawing lines on the chart. I was busy trying to draw a trend line to mark of a compression zone, I accidentily picked up my SL line (not sure how as it was far away from where I was working), I didn't what to change my SL so I moved my cursor out of the window thinking that MT4 would not execute the change. It did execute the change and I suddenly got stop out at the wrong place. Something to be aware of.
